P1.evidence: Setter notes referenced at the open and used again mid-call on nutrition — 'I heard from Kim, you're not eating like a lot of junk food or anything, you have home-cooked' — which is the check working as intended. Frame remains three-part, missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement asked and given, and the standard open question ran, then was usefully sharpened when the prospect answered vaguely: 'As in, like, what are you specifically trying to achieve?'

P2.evidence: Work was properly established and mined — the rep named the occupation, confirmed it, and then dug out the single most important operational constraint on the call, that January to April is unworkable and he leaves the house at 7am and gets back at 9-10pm. The injury probe ran well too, establishing the lower back as chronic, currently aches not pain, and self-limiting (he avoids deadlifts). Diet was probed to real specifics, pushing past 'I eat home food' to the daily four-or-five-spoons of sugar and weekend sodas. Against that: age, height and weight were all volunteered in his opening monologue and never asked, so they do not credit. Health conditions were never asked of a 56-year-old, sleep was never mentioned, and energy was never asked.

P3.evidence: The aesthetics question ran cleanly — 'When it comes to getting into better shape for you, what does that mean? Is that just getting a six-pack or describe that for you?' — and the trigger question ran twice and worked, surfacing that his time freed up and that his wife's surgery made him not want to 'stay behind'. The rep also asked the good disqualifying question, 'a lot of people around 50 to 60 say I'll do it later — why is that not you?'. The gap is P3f, and it is expensive: he had already named a 15-years-younger wife, two young children and a circle of run-down friends, and was never asked who else this impacts. Building the wife into the why would have pre-empted the spouse objection that later ended the call. The reflect-back at 00:12:32 listed his goals accurately but never made the 'this isn't really about the weight' turn.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase in the batch so far and the model for how this should run. Past attempts asked and surfaced ('you mentioned you haven't done anything like this before, right?' → CrossFit 2018-19), then interrogated ('CrossFit, why would you just go back into that?' → too energy-driven, not muscle-focused). The blocker question was asked directly — 'what's the reason that you feel like, why don't I just do it with someone one-on-one instead of just trying to figure it out on your own?' — and then the P4f check ran almost verbatim: 'there's always videos online, but what's the reason that you're not going to follow videos online?' The prospect named the gap himself, repeatedly and in his own words: 'a little motivation, it's really probably one of the things', 'have motivation, have the structure, I think it's psychological', 'It's when I don't have anything organized that it's on and off.' Only P4c is soft — the reasons offered were circumstantial (kids, COVID, projects) and the rep accepted them rather than pressing on the pattern.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran close to script — 'Would you be able to settle for not getting to that point for yourself, where you sort of stay the exact same way as it currently is going for the next few years?' — and the rep had already set up a consequence image the prospect supplied himself, his friends being 'run down at this point, and I don't want to get to that point'. He probed it once: 'Do you feel like you would get to that point if you don't really take action on it?' But the prospect deflected ('I don't know if I get to that point, because I'm always doing something') and the rep did not push, then answered his own question with the 70-year-olds contrast instead of asking 'why not'. The line in the sand was asserted, not requested: 'It sounds like you're ready to go. It sounds like you just want to make a decision for yourself and get on with it.'

P6.evidence: P6b ran — 'do you feel like when we get that in place, there would be anything missing to get you to the point where...' — and got 'so far, I don't think so'. But the belief check drew a distinctly soft answer, 'That's what I hope, yeah', which is not a clear yes, and the rep moved to price anyway. P6c then failed a second time: when hesitation surfaced the playbook says return to Phase 5, and instead the rep went into instalment arithmetic.

P11.evidence: No agreement reached, so payment and onboarding were unreachable. Credit where due on the adjacent behaviour: the rep did book a specific follow-up for the next day at 5pm and confirmed the calendar invite arrived live, which is the right move when the close cannot land.

objection_plays.detail: Clear trigger — 'I do have to discuss it with my wife anyway'. One move ran, and ran twice: the personal-commitment isolation, 'do you personally feel like, yeah, I do want to make it work, and I see myself making it work?' and 'just from the top of your head, do you feel like it is something that would be workable, it just comes down to figuring it out with your wife?'. Everything else was skipped — no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger and less in pain', no ownership question, no deposit-and-go-talk-to-her fallback. Worse, the rep twice joked about being made to sleep on the couch, which reinforces the wife's veto rather than reframing it. Note the play would need adapting here: she is a fellow accountant who jointly manages the household bills, so the scripted 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' line would have been wrong and possibly damaging.

Trigger at 00:59:11, 'the numbers is a little high... The issue for me is the money part, because we're full of bills'. The best move on the call ran: the won't-versus-can't isolation, 'is it more of like, I just don't want to do it all up front, or is it more so I just can't?'. The instalment option was offered, which is the scripted move. But no financial picture was taken at all — no cash on hand, no leftover after bills beyond what he volunteered, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments — and no 'are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially'. The prospect volunteered his ceiling unprompted ($1,000/month) and the rep responded by quoting $1,200/month, which is the opposite of making it work. The play was also muddied by contradictory instalment terms the prospect had to query.

'I really got to think about it now' at 00:57:31, plus 'I think I need to sleep over on this one'. The rep isolated and secured a next call, which is a legitimate handling, but none of the OA moves proper ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. Booking tomorrow at 5pm is worth more than a botched OA here, so this is a defensible partial rather than a failure.

Script gap: a proof and credibility objection. 'How do I see something that I could be more assured that this is the program?... it's nothing but a reel and a conversation and going into a $3,000 $6,000 deal almost immediately.' This is not price, timing, spouse, thinking or fear — it is a stranger being asked for thousands 24 hours after first seeing a video, and there is no play for it. The rep isolated it correctly and improvised a screenshare of Instagram testimonials, but had to concede 'there is not much more' to show. A prospect this legitimate deserves a proof asset, and the script should have a route for a same-day-lead trust objection.

Second script gap: an unaddressed contraindication. He stated he must avoid movements that aggravate his lower back and named deadlifts specifically. Kettlebell training is built on the hip hinge. Nobody confirmed the programme can work around it, and the presentation actually promised a mobility routine 'specifically made to you and to of course your lower back' without any qualification. There is no scripted step for checking whether the movement library fits the body in front of you.
No timing objection — the opposite, he volunteered that this is the best window he has had in years and that the three-week holiday starting tomorrow is ideal for building the habit.
No fear or doubt about the programme working; he explicitly ruled it out: 'I don't have any doubts on Trevor and in his program.'

notes: The discovery here was the best in the batch — Phase 4 ran almost to script and the prospect named his own gap three separate ways, which is exactly the ammunition needed at the close. It was then spent badly. Two fixable errors: nobody was ever brought into the why, so the wife arrived at the end as a pure obstacle rather than as a reason; and the instalment terms were quoted so inconsistently that the prospect had to correct the rep, landing on $1,200/month against a stated $1,000/month ceiling. Coach the numbers cold before the next call, lead the follow-up with the wife as beneficiary rather than approver, and go in with something concrete to show him — he asked for proof and got 'there is not much more'.
